en: The Scripture on the Ghost’s Questioning of Maudgalyāyana, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Bamboo Grove of Kalandaka in Rājagṛha. At that time...
In the afternoon, Maudgalyāyana arose from meditative concentration and was wandering along the banks of the Ganges when he saw various hungry ghosts undergoing different forms of retribution.
Upon seeing the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, the hungry ghosts all conceived a heart of reverence and came forward to inquire about the causes and conditions of their plight.
One ghost asked, "Since my birth,
I have constantly suffered from headaches.
What sin has caused this?"
Maudgalyāyana replied, "When you were a human being, you delighted in striking the heads of sentient beings with a staff.
Now you receive this 'flower-retribution'; as for the 'fruit,' you shall enter hell."
One ghost asked: "Since my birth, I have possessed immeasurable wealth and resources, yet I take pleasure in wearing tattered clothes.
What sin has caused this?"
Maudgalyāyana replied:
"When you were a human being, you practiced giving and performed meritorious deeds, yet you later regretted and begrudged them.
Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
A ghost asked: "Since my birth, I have had no fixed dwelling place and have always leaned against the lanes and streets.
What sin has caused this?"
Maudgalyāyana replied, “When you were a human being,
when guests came seeking lodging, you refused to provide them with a place to stay;
yet, seeing others providing lodging to guests, you became angry and resentful.”
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; as for the fruit, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked, "I eat more than a *hu* of food, yet I cannot be satiated."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you fed sentient beings but never allowed them to be satisfied."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; the fruit will be to enter hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since birth, my belly has been as large as a jar, yet my throat is as narrow as the eye of a needle, so that I cannot swallow food."
"By what offense was this caused?

Maudgalyāyana replied, "When you were a human being, you served as the head of a village. Relying on your own power and arrogance, you treated the common people with contempt and deceit; you would forcibly beat those who offended you and demand fine, delicious food."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; eventually, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked, "Since my birth, I have constantly suffered from a festering ulcer on my male organ, the pain of which is beyond description."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you committed sexual misconduct in a pure place, such as a Buddhist stūpa or monastery."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; for its fruit, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since my birth, I have had many sons; they were all handsome and pleasing, yet all died young."
Thinking of this, my heart is severed with grief; the pain is beyond words.
What sin has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied:
"When you were a human being, you saw your child kill a living creature, and you rejoiced in it and ate the meat;
because of the killing, he will have a short life, and because of your rejoicing, you will suffer bitter agony.
Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' and as its fruit, you shall enter hell."
One ghost asked: "Since my birth, there has been a dog with a massive body and sharp teeth, its two eyes blazing red, that constantly comes to devour me."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you delighted in hunting with dogs, harming sentient beings without any heart of compassion."
"Now you receive the floral retribution; the fruit awaits you in hell. Another ghost asked:

"Since I was born, there has been a man who constantly carries various sharp knives to slice off my flesh; once it is all gone, he takes it away. In a mere moment, it grows back and he comes again to cut it. The pain is beyond description."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied, "When you were a human being,
you delighted in slaughtering and dismembering sentient beings, never possessing a heart of compassion."
"Now you receive this as the 'flower reward,' and for its fruit, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since my birth, I have constantly suffered from ailments; every part of my body aches, and the pain is unbearable."
"What offense has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied, "When you were a human being, you delighted in fishing and hunting; you would cast the fish caught in your nets onto the sand and soil, causing them to die in agony."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; as for the fruit, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked, "Since my birth, I have been dull-witted and possessed no knowledge."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you forcibly urged others to drink wine, causing them to fall into confusion."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; the fruit will be entry into hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since my birth, I have constantly suffered from heat and thirst. While traveling, I saw the Ganges River and hoped to enter it to relieve my heat and thirst."
As soon as they enter within, their bodies become scorched and rotted, and their flesh falls away from their bones;
when they are thirsty and wish to drink, even a single mouthful that enters the belly causes the five viscera to burn and rot, with a pain beyond description.
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you delighted in burning mountains and marshes, thereby harming and killing living beings."
"Now you receive this as the flower-retribution; the fruit will be that you enter hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since I was born, I have constantly suffered from hunger and thirst. I wish to go to the latrine to take some excrement and eat it."
"On this latrine there is a powerful ghost who strikes me with a staff; at first, he could not even get near me.
What sin has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied:
"When you were a human being, you served as the master of a Buddhist monastery (*stūpa*).
When visiting bhikṣus arrived, you were stingy and refused to give them food;
only after the guests had departed did you provide it to the resident monks."
"Because you were stingy with the property of the Sangha, you now receive this 'flower-retribution,' and as its fruit, you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since birth, I have always dwelt in impurity; foulness and affliction envelop my body, and I cannot escape them."
"At a time of hunger and thirst, you must eat this impurity again.
What sin has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied:
"When you were a human being, you were the son of a brahmin.
At that time, there was a practitioner who came to you for alms later in the day.
You then employed a stratagem so that this practitioner would not come to beg again: you took his bowl, filled the bottom with excrement, and covered it over with rice."

The practitioner took the bowl and returned to his original place; having set it down on one side and finished rinsing his mouth, he gathered the bowl intending to eat, but the contents were so foul and filthy that he could not even approach it.
"For this reason, you have fallen into hell; in a future life, you shall fall into the Piśāca-mīḍha (Feces and Urine) Hell.
Another ghost asked:
"Since birth, there has been a copper pitcher upon my shoulder, filled to the brim with molten copper."
"With one hand he grasps a copper ladle to scoop it up, then pours it back over his own head; the pain is beyond description.
What sin has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied:
"When you were a human being, you served as the *karmadāna* of the Saṃgha and managed its affairs.
You had a jar of ghee stored away in another place; instead of distributing it to the Saṃgha, you waited until the guests had departed before finally giving it to the resident monks."
"This ghee is the property of the Saṃgha of the four quarters; all have a share in it.
Because you were stingy with the property of the Saṃgha, you now receive this as the 'flower-retribution,' and for its 'fruit,' you shall enter hell.
Another ghost asked:

"Throughout my entire life, I have ascended the mountain of blades and the forest of swords in hell, or fallen into the pit of fire and the cauldron of boiling water in hell; I have endured various sufferings without any respite."
"By what offense was this caused?

Maudgalyāyana replied, "When you were a human being, you served as the master of a celestial shrine. You slaughtered the three sacrificial animals to offer to the heavenly deities, drenching the four directions with their blood and flesh, and said to the multitude:"
"You shall obtain great fortune and prosperity through these sacrifices!
Thus they utter such demonic and heterodox words, such wicked and seductive speech, to lightly deceive the common people and delude their parents.
"For this reason, I have entered hell.
Another ghost asked,
"Since my birth, I have constantly swallowed iron balls."
"By what offense was this caused?
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"When you were a human being, you were a śrāmaṇera who took pure water to make stone-honey syrup."
The rock honey was hard and large, yet you stole and broke off a small portion;
because you stole and ate a single mouthful before the Sangha had eaten,
by this causal condition, you have entered hell as a result, and in future lives you shall constantly swallow iron balls.
At that time, after Maudgalyāyana had finished reciting the Sūtra on Past Causes and Conditions for the hungry ghosts, he returned to Vulture Peak Mountain.
The entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, prostrated themselves and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra on the Ghost’s Questioning of Maudgalyāyana Spoken by the Buddha.
